posts.title: What we ask on the first call
posts.excerpt: Our first video conversation lasts forty-five minutes and focuses on the quiet questions that help us understand how you travel together.
posts.content:
When couples join our video call from their kitchen table or living room, they often expect a sales presentation with glossy brochures and predefined packages. Instead, our forty-five-minute call begins with open space and quiet listening. Aiko Brandt founded Futari Journeys in 2014 on the principle that tailor-made travel should never start with an itinerary; it must start with the two people travelling. Whether you speak with Aiko, Mateus Okafor, or Lina Haddad, the initial consultation is entirely free, scheduled Monday to Saturday between 09:00 and 19:00 CET.

The first question we ask is deceptively simple: what does a restful morning look like for each of you? One partner might picture waking up early for an espresso on a guesthouse balcony before taking a coastal path, while the other envisions sleeping late and lingering over fresh bread with no fixed schedule. Uncovering these differing rhythms early on allows us to design a route where neither person feels hurried or held back. A journey succeeds not by packing every hour with activities, but by finding a shared pace that lets both travellers relax.

Next, we discuss timing and landscape rather than specific countries. If you are planning a honeymoon, we recommend starting four to nine months ahead, whereas six weeks is plenty of time for an anniversary weekend. Many couples arrive at the call knowing only the calendar month they can take off from work. We might discuss how May brings blooming hydrangeas and crater lake mist to the Azores, how September offers calm rail travel between Slovenian mountains and the sea, or why October brings warm, golden light to olive groves in Puglia.

We also speak openly about budget expectations during this initial forty-five minutes. Our studio charges fixed planning fees: €290 for an anniversary weekend of two to four nights, €450 for a short escape of five to seven nights, €780 for a honeymoon of eight to sixteen nights, and €1,150 for a long journey of seventeen to thirty nights across two or more countries. Adding surprise planning is €120. Most honeymoons we design total between €6,000 and €14,000 for two, including flights. Because we take zero commission from hotels, we pass every trade rate and seasonal saving directly to you.

Finally, we outline what happens after you close your laptop. Within seven days, we send you an initial tailored route outline along with our fee confirmation. You have two rounds of revisions to adjust travel times, destinations, and accommodation styles. In our Valmere studio on Linden Row, Jonas Weber coordinates bookings, Priya Nair verifies passport validity and visa requirements, and Ren Ishida hand-draws your route map. Fourteen days before departure, your printed travel kit arrives in the post, and Camille Laurent ensures our travel-day line is available twenty-four hours a day until you return.

We intentionally accept about forty trips each year, allowing us to build genuine relationships with every couple we guide. If you have questions about how a route comes together, booking a planning call is simple. Bring whatever thoughts or dates you have, and we will take the time to listen.
